open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether an evaluated representation with state count and bit complexity \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) is closed under arbitrary heterogeneous cutoff-forest branching, component multiplication, moving ordered-core endpoints, and all zero-, one-, and two-tag coefficient extractions remains open.
open_obligations.obstruction: On an ascending core-priority chamber, a heterogeneous component with branch exponents \(a_{ji}\) and center weight \(c_j\) has nonconstant cutoff terms carrying the future profile \(c_j+A_{jr},\ldots,c_j+A_{jk}\), where \(A_{jr}=\sum_{i\le r}a_{ji}\). For \(k=2\), the profiles \(1,1\) and \(1,2\) give \(T_{11}=1/3+(t_1^2/2+1/6)t_2^3\) and \(T_{12}=1/4+(t_1^2/2+1/4)t_2^4\). Activating the \(t_1\)-dependent term in either factor leaves the same current exponent but different future exponents. Thus relative core order, a scalar activation count, and a current-degree total are not closed states; retaining all \(k\) degree totals gives the forbidden \((nb)^{\Theta(k)}\) behavior. The vertex-cover subset dynamic program does not remove this obstruction: its scalar set functional \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)\) is available only because every exterior component is a single vertex, whereas heterogeneous forest messages carry distinct future-prefix exponent profiles created by branching and moving-endpoint integration.
open_obligations.attempted: The three-state recursion and \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion were reduced to chamber polynomials. For vertex-cover cores, chamber enumeration was replaced by the subset recurrence \(D[S\cup\{f\}]\mathrel{+}=D[S]/(|S|+1+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S\cup\{f\}))\), which closes because the cumulative exponent is determined by the entered core subset \(S\). Identical replicated-star attachments were compressed by the one-index nested-moment recurrence. Expanding that recurrence for the two heterogeneous profiles above fails because equal current states leave different future exponents. Dense chamber-polynomial evaluation closes arbitrary forest branching, component products, moving endpoints, and tags, but costs \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) rather than fixed-parameter time.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved partial result is a complete evaluated XP algorithm for arbitrary feedback forests with cost \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\), together with a vertex-cover subset dynamic program using \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations and polynomial intermediate rational bit length, and an \(O(k!km^2)\)-operation recurrence for identical replicated-star attachments. These results leave no unevaluated integration gate, but they do not provide the requested general heterogeneous fixed-parameter closure.

prose_updates.tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but published AWRI rule selection relies on simulation. Conditioning on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set and applying a three-state forest recursion with \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion yields an exact, fully evaluated dense algorithm for every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law in \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bit operations. The tagged laws reconstruct every dense RDIM risk matrix. Rational weak semidefinite optimization then returns an independently checkable \(\varepsilon\)-minimax certificate in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\); for canonical \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\), this dependence is polynomial in \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\). When the supplied core is a vertex cover, a subset dynamic program eliminates explicit chamber enumeration and computes all tagged laws in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. An evaluated recurrence also covers identical replicated-star attachments, but fixed-parameter closure for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains open.

project_justification.gap: AWRI fixes the weighted greedy design and balanced RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate. Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, while structural graph programs count static sets. General semidefinite design methods neither supply the exact WRI/RDIM risk matrices nor give this end-to-end rational certificate with complexity measured against the actual binary encoding of an arbitrary rational tolerance. None of these results gives the evaluated heterogeneous tagged integration used here. The subset dynamic program closes the vertex-cover special case in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, but arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments still lack a fixed-parameter representation.
project_justification.niche: A supplied feedback set exposes a forest decomposition on which exact heterogeneous priority integration is possible. The proved general guarantee is XP in the feedback size. If the supplied core is a vertex cover, cumulative priority exponents depend only on the entered core subset, yielding an \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) subset dynamic program with polynomial rational height; identical attachment profiles give a second evaluated special regime. Once the exact rational risk library is available, the finite ellipsoidal risk game admits a rational primal-dual certificate whose computation is polynomial in the encoded tolerance; for dyadic tolerance \(2^{-p}\), it is polynomial in \(p\).
project_justification.fill: The paper proves core inclusion--exclusion, a fully evaluated dense chamber-polynomial algorithm with controlled rational bit height, exact tagged RDIM risk reconstruction, and a rational near-minimax certificate. It also replaces factorial chamber enumeration in the vertex-cover subclass by a subset dynamic program with \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit complexity and polynomial intermediate rational height. The certificate algorithm is polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\), specializing to polynomial dependence on \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\) for canonical dyadic input \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\). The paper records arbitrary-forest fixed-parameter moment closure as an open problem rather than assuming it.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li supply the published directed-network FNI/TTE/WRI plus balanced-RDIM causal-design construction used here. This note first identifies WRI deletion with greedy maximal-independent-set selection on the neighborhood-overlap conflict graph, and then proves exact algorithms only for the positive-integer-weight subclass with a supplied feedback set. Positive rational priority weights transfer by multiplying all exponential, equivalently Beta, rates by a common denominator, which preserves their random order; arbitrary published real weights are not covered by the exact Turing-model algorithms. Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li derive a balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate and use simulation for candidate-weight selection. Pippenger's random-sequential-adsorption recursions, Gamarnik and Goldberg's rooted-tree bonus recursions, and the local-limit equations of Krivelevich, Meszaros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman do not compute exact finite heterogeneous tagged moments. Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li count static independent sets on bounded-treewidth graphs, and Borie, Parker, and Tovey give finite-state decomposition methods, but neither weights maximal independent sets by heterogeneous priority orders. Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk establish a \(2^{O(k\log k)}\) scale for a different feedback-set problem, not an oracle for the present integration. The present \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) vertex-cover bound instead follows from a problem-specific subset dynamic program for cumulative cutoff exponents; it does not settle heterogeneous forest closure. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje study an unrestricted network-experiment minimax functional; no equality with that functional is claimed. Kallus motivates mixed minimax design, and Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong develop semidefinite minimax-design methods. Boyd and Vandenberghe supply the finite-dimensional separating-hyperplane theorem and its open-set converse used in the minimax interchange. Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver's Theorem 4.3.13 supplies weak constrained convex minimization for centered convex bodies given by weak-membership and convex-function value oracles; the rational affine-SDP parametrization, radius bounds, membership tests, and pullback needed here are proved separately in this note. Aronow and Samii provide the design-based interference framework. Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet motivate the rural-China insurance application but provide no evidence that its measured conflict graph has small feedback number or a small vertex cover.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact algorithm removes Monte Carlo error from comparison of prespecified WRI rules, but its worst-case general cost is XP rather than fixed-parameter in the feedback number. If a measured conflict graph comes with a small vertex-cover core, the subset dynamic program gives the sharper \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) exact computation with polynomial intermediate rational bit length; identical repeated attachments admit a separate evaluated recurrence. Neither special case establishes fixed-parameter tractability for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments. The final semidefinite certificate concerns worst-case squared error of the fixed RDIM rule library over the stated endpoint ellipsoid; it is not a claim of optimality among all network designs or estimators.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The dense chamber-polynomial representation closes arbitrary heterogeneous branching, component products, moving endpoints, and tags, but uses \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) states. It therefore proves an evaluated XP theorem, not the originally proposed fixed-parameter theorem. The vertex-cover subset state \(S\subseteq\mathcal K\) suffices because every exterior component is a single vertex and its cumulative exponent is the scalar functional \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)\); branching forest components instead retain distinct future ordered-ratio exponent profiles. Two heterogeneous branches can have the same present activation count and exponent while leaving different exponents on future variables. The unresolved question is whether a shared operator representation can preserve those profiles in \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) time. A table indexed by \(k\) degree totals, a profile-count vector with an \(n\)-dependent exponent, or a circuit retaining an integration gate does not solve that question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general proved result assumes a supplied feedback set, positive integer priority weights, and permits XP dependence \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\); it neither finds a minimum feedback set nor proves arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability. The \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) fixed-parameter guarantee with polynomial rational height requires that the supplied feedback core also be a vertex cover, and the other evaluated special result concerns the stated identical replicated-star coefficient. Nondegenerate isolation is required only for RDIM denominators and risk reconstruction. The minimax result chooses within a prespecified WRI/RDIM library over a graph-Sobolev endpoint ellipsoid and does not equal the unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional. The rural-China follow-up is a prospective consumer, not evidence for a small empirical feedback number, a small vertex cover, a calibrated ellipsoid, or improved field performance.

statement_notes.justification: This is the isolated open question separating the proved dense XP algorithm from arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability. The new vertex-cover subset dynamic program sharpens a special case to \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations but does not resolve heterogeneous forest closure.
statement_notes.gap: Heterogeneous branches preserve distinct future ordered-ratio exponent profiles. Unlike the vertex-cover case, those profiles are not determined by the entered core subset alone, and no fixed-parameter-size state algebra is proved to close them.
statement_notes.consumer: A future solution would sharpen the general XP bound; current design recommendations may use the proved XP evaluator or the \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) vertex-cover oracle and do not rely on the unresolved general sharpening.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N(v)=N_{C_G}(v)\) and \(N(H)=\bigcup_{u\in H}N(u)\).  Because \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover, \(V\setminus\mathcal K\) is edgeless.  The case \(k=0\) is therefore immediate: \(C_G\) is edgeless, the greedy rule selects all of \(V\), and
\[
 F_{\ell,A}(z)=z^n
 \qquad (|A|\leq 2).
\]
This requires only polynomial output time and introduces no nonintegral intermediate quantity.  Henceforth let \(k\geq1\).

Fix a rule \(\ell\), an independent set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\), and a set \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U\).  Define
\[
 W_{\mathcal U}=(V\setminus\mathcal K)\cap N(\mathcal U),
 \qquad
 T_{\mathcal U}=(V\setminus\mathcal K)\setminus N(\mathcal U),
 \qquad
 S_{\mathcal U}=\mathcal U\cup T_{\mathcal U}.
\]
If a greedy output has intersection \(\mathcal U\) with the core, independence excludes every vertex of \(W_{\mathcal U}\).  Conversely, every vertex of \(T_{\mathcal U}\) must be selected: if such a vertex were unselected, the domination direction of \(\texttt{lem:greedy-domination-certificate}\) would give it an earlier selected neighbor, but it has no neighbor in \(\mathcal U\) and has no neighbor in \(V\setminus\mathcal K\).  Thus \(S_{\mathcal U}\) is the only possible greedy output with core intersection \(\mathcal U\).  In particular, the contribution indexed by \(\mathcal U\) vanishes unless \(A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\).

We next evaluate that contribution.  Since the exterior graph is edgeless, every rooted component in \(\texttt{def:cutoff-forest-messages}\) is a singleton.  For an untagged \(v\in W_{\mathcal U}\), the selected message is zero and the singleton component factor is
\[
 \int_0^1 B_v(y,z)\,dy
 =\int_0^{p_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =p_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}},
 \qquad
 p_v(x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal U\cap N(v)}x_u.
\]
For \(v\in T_{\mathcal U}\), one has \(p_v(x)=0\), so \(C_v(y,z)=h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\) and \(B_v(y,z)=0\); its factor, whether or not it is tagged, is
\[
 \int_0^1 A_v(y,z)\,dy
 =z\int_0^{r_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =z r_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}},
 \qquad
 r_v(x)=\min\bigl(\{x_f:f\in\mathcal B\cap N(v)\}\cup\{1\}\bigr).
\]
If a tagged exterior vertex lies in \(W_{\mathcal U}\), the instruction \(B_v=C_v=0\) in that definition makes the factor zero.  Together with the core-tag restriction in \(\texttt{def:core-inclusion-exclusion}\), these observations give exactly the gate \(\mathbf 1\{A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\}\).  Therefore \(\texttt{prop:core-inclusion-exclusion}\) reduces to the explicit finite formula
\[
 F_{\ell,A}(z)
 =\sum_{\substack{\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\ {
m independent}\\ A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}}}
 z^{|S_{\mathcal U}|}
 \sum_{\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U}
 (-1)^{|\mathcal B|} I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B},                                      \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
 I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B}
 ={}&\int_{(0,1)^{\mathcal K}}
 \chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(x)
 \prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}x_f^{h_{\ell f}-1}
 \prod_{v\in W_{\mathcal U}}
 \left(\max_{u\in\mathcal U\cap N(v)}x_u\right)^{h_{\ell v}}\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\cdot
 \prod_{v\in T_{\mathcal U}}
 \left(\min\bigl(\{x_f:f\in\mathcal B\cap N(v)\}\cup\{1\}\bigr)\right)^{h_{\ell v}}\,dx .       \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
All powers in (2) are nonnegative integers because \(1\leq h_{\ell i}\leq b\).

It remains to evaluate (2) without enumerating the \(k!\) order chambers.  For \(f\in\mathcal K\), put
\[
 \operatorname{Pred}(f)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathcal U\cap N(f),&f\in\mathcal B,\\
 \varnothing,&f\notin\mathcal B,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for \(S\subseteq\mathcal K\), define the integer
\[
\begin{split}
 E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)={}&
 \sum_{f\in S}(h_{\ell f}-1)
 +\sum_{\substack{v\in W_{\mathcal U}\\
                    \mathcal U\cap N(v)\subseteq S}}h_{\ell v}
 +\sum_{\substack{v\in T_{\mathcal U}\\
                    \mathcal B\cap N(v)\cap S\neq\varnothing}}h_{\ell v}.                 \tag{3}
\end{split}
\]
Partition the cube, up to its measure-zero tie set, into ascending chambers
\[
 0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1.
\]
The continuous beta densities in \(\texttt{def:wri-law}\) assign zero mass to the omitted tie set.  On a chamber, \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}=1\) precisely when every \(u\in\operatorname{Pred}(f)\) occurs before \(f\).  Indeed, these are exactly the inequalities \(x_u<x_f\) appearing in the definition of \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}\).

Let \(S_r=\{\sigma(1),\ldots,\sigma(r)\}\).  After removing the constant factor \(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\), the integrand on this chamber is a monomial.  The sum of the exponents attached to coordinates in its prefix \(S_r\) is exactly \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S_r)\): the core-density exponent \(h_{\ell f}-1\) has entered exactly when \(f\in S_r\); a maximum over \(\mathcal U\cap N(v)\) has entered exactly when all of its arguments are in \(S_r\); and a nonconstant minimum over \(\mathcal B\cap N(v)\) has entered exactly when at least one of its arguments is in \(S_r\).  If the chamber monomial is \(\prod_{j=1}^k x_{\sigma(j)}^{a_j}\), repeated integration from the smallest coordinate outward gives
\[
 \int_{0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1}
 \prod_{j=1}^k x_{\sigma(j)}^{a_j}\,dx
 =\prod_{r=1}^k
 \frac{1}{r+\sum_{j=1}^r a_j}
 =\prod_{r=1}^k\frac{1}{r+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S_r)}.                    \tag{4}
\]
The first equality follows inductively from \(\int_0^t x^a\,dx=t^{a+1}/(a+1)\).  Every denominator in (4) is positive, since it is at least \(r\geq1\).

Define a subset dynamic program by
\[
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[\varnothing]=1
\]
and, for every \(S\subsetneq\mathcal K\) and \(f\in\mathcal K\setminus S\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Pred}(f)\subseteq S\), perform
\[
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[S\cup\{f\}]
 \mathrel{+}=
 \frac{D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[S]}
 {|S|+1+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S\cup\{f\})}.                              \tag{5}
\]
Induction on \(|S|\) shows that the stored value is the sum, over all allowed orderings of \(S\), of the product of the factors in (4) along that ordering.  The transition condition is exactly the predecessor condition for appending \(f\).  At \(S=\mathcal K\), the allowed orderings are therefore exactly the chambers on which \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}=1\).  Equations (2)--(5) consequently prove
\[
 I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B}
 =\left(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\right)
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[\mathcal K].                                      \tag{6}
\]
Thus (1), (3), (5), and (6) are an evaluated rational algorithm for every coefficient and contain no residual integral.

There are at most
\[
 \sum_{\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K}2^{k-|\mathcal U|}=3^k
\]
pairs \((\mathcal U,\mathcal B)\); restricting \(\mathcal U\) to independent sets only decreases this number.  For a fixed pair, direct tabulation of (3) for all subsets and all transitions in (5) uses \(2^k\operatorname{poly}(n,k,\lambda)\) operations.  The contribution for a pair is written to the at most \(1+n+\binom n2\) tags passing \(A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\).  Repeating over \(L\) rules therefore uses
\[
 L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)                                         \tag{7}
\]
rational operations, including all tag tests and coefficient accumulation.

For the bit bound, let \(D'=k(nb+1)\) and \(M=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,D')\).  For a transition reaching a set \(S\) of size \(r\), its denominator is
\[
 q(S)=r+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S).
\]
The two exterior sets partition \(V\setminus\mathcal K\), so (3) and \(h_{\ell i}\leq b\) yield
\[
 1\leq q(S)
 \leq r+r(b-1)+(n-k)b
 \leq nb
 \leq D'.                                                                     \tag{8}
\]
Hence every path denominator through layer \(r\) divides \(M^r\).  Implement (5) by storing every layer-\(r\) value over the common denominator \(M^r\).  Since there are at most \(r!\) paths to a state and every factor in (4) is at most one, its numerator in this representation has absolute value at most \(r!M^r\).  Moreover,
\[
 \log M\leq\log(D'!)\leq D'\log D'.                                          \tag{9}
\]
After multiplication by \(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\), summing at most \(3^k\) signed pair contributions over the common denominator \(M^k\) adds at most
\[
 O\bigl(k\log 3+k\log b+\log(k!)+kD'\log D'\bigr)                            \tag{10}
\]
bits.  This is polynomial in \(n,b,\lambda\), because \(k\leq n\).  Thus all arithmetic in (7) has polynomial bit cost, and (7) is also a bit-operation bound.

As an exact smallest-instance check, take \(n=2\), \(\mathcal K=\{f\}\), and one exterior neighbor \(v\).  Formula (5) gives probability \(h_{\ell f}/(h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v})\) to \(S=\{f\}\) and its complement to \(S=\{v\}\), agreeing with the direct integral
\[
 \Pr(X_{\ell f}>X_{\ell v})
 =\int_0^1h_{\ell f}x^{h_{\ell f}-1}x^{h_{\ell v}}\,dx
 =\frac{h_{\ell f}}{h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v}}.
\]
Consequently \(F_{\ell,\varnothing}(z)=z\), \(F_{\ell,\{f\}}(z)=zh_{\ell f}/(h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v})\), \(F_{\ell,\{v\}}(z)=zh_{\ell v}/(h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v})\), and \(F_{\ell,\{f,v\}}(z)=0\), checking all zero-, one-, and two-tags.  At the opposite boundary \(k=n\), the exterior sums in (3) vanish and (8) still leaves every divisor at least one, so the argument does not rely on a nonempty exterior.

We have proved the sharper running time (7) and polynomial intermediate rational height.  Finally, for \(k\geq1\), \(2^k\leq2k!\), so \(6^k\leq2k!3^k\); the case \(k=0\) was handled separately.  Hence the theorem's stated \(Lk!3^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) running-time bound follows, and the polynomial height bound is stronger than \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\).
